source_user: A long-context workload intermittently hits OOM after several concurrent requests. Give a prioritized diagnosis and mitigations. Scenario variant 237: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure per-request KV growth and allocator fragmentation; check max sequence and batch; inspect active sequences; test paged/prefix cache, admission control, quantization, and context limits.
corrected_answer:
Treat corpus-01537 (scenario variant 237) as an underspecified intermittent serving incident. Assume the framework, accelerator model/count, model architecture, dtype, parallelism, allocator, scheduler, cache policy, quotas, and memory limits are unknown; do not claim a root cause without measurements. First preserve request IDs and timestamps and classify each event as device OOM, host/pinned/shared-memory exhaustion, swap pressure, runtime/driver failure, or admission/quota rejection. Record versions, configuration, phase (prefill/decode), cancellation status, and whether the failure is per-request or node-wide.

Prioritize diagnosis in repeated, matched strata of prompt length, generated length, concurrency, batch/prefill size, and request mix. Collect per-request token counts and KV bytes/growth, active sequences, allocated and reserved device bytes, free headroom and largest free block, fragmentation, temporary workspace and collective buffers, cache residency/retention/eviction and cleanup delay, host RSS/pinned/shared memory, swap, queueing, latency, and error denominators. Check configured versus effective maximum sequence/context and batch limits, scheduler admission, and whether paged or prefix caching is actually enabled. Keep measured bytes separate from estimates and use explicit bytes/GiB units.

Falsifiable hypothesis: at the observed concurrency, live KV growth plus transient workspace exceeds usable device headroom; if true, pre-failure KV/headroom trajectories and OOM rates will rise with live tokens, and reducing live-token admission while holding workload strata constant will reduce OOMs without changing correctness. Run a randomized, blocked A/B experiment across the strata: baseline versus a conservative token-and-memory admission cap, with identical prompts, max output limits, model/runtime versions, warm-up, cache state, and load schedule. Repeat enough times for uncertainty intervals; compare OOM, rejection, timeout, cancellation, throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, utilization, and correctness. Falsify the hypothesis if matched failures do not track KV/headroom or if the cap does not reduce OOMs. Test competing explanations separately: fragmentation, workspace/collective spikes, cache leakage/retention, host pressure, scheduler/accounting bugs, and device/host communication failures.

Immediate safeguards: stop increasing concurrency, cap context/output tokens using measured headroom, reject or queue safely before allocation, bound cache retention, and clean up cancelled requests. Do not enable quantization, prefix/paged caching, or lower context limits as an unmeasured fix: evaluate one change at a time and verify numerical/correctness behavior. Canary changes with explicit rollback gates (any correctness regression, error-rate increase, SLO breach, or unexplained host/device pressure); retain logs and revert on threshold breach. Evidence required before declaring cause or capacity: correlated traces and allocator snapshots across repeated randomized runs, version/configuration capture, and expert review; this provisional assessment cannot establish platform-wide capacity.
